title: Compatibility scoring and regional safety lattice for deployment rollouts
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Background:
Redwood needs an automated decision layer that evaluates new model variants during progressive rollouts and decides whether to advance, pause, reroute, or fully rollback. Current rollout logic uses simple SLO checks (latency + error rate) and static compatibility flags; this ticket introduces a compatibility scoring service plus a regional safety lattice that combines compatibility, capacity, and semantic-quality signals to make deterministic routing and fallback decisions during canary/A-B/shadow deployments.

Problem statement:
- Newer model variants can pass coarse SLOs while having subtle regressions (semantic drift, hallucination increase) that our current checks miss.
- Region-specific capacity or preemption events require different levels of confidence before increasing traffic in that region.
- We need a single, auditable decision surface for rollout actions that operates across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Goals:
1) Define a compatibility score (0-100) for a model variant per region that aggregates schema compatibility, KV-cache binary compatibility, tokenizer/version differences, quantization compatibility, and known-issue flags.
2) Build a safety lattice: per-region safety states (GREEN / YELLOW / RED) computed from compatibility score, reserved capacity headroom, and live quality metrics (P95 latency, error rate, and semantic-eval delta).
3) Integrate the scorer and lattice into the canary controller so rollout decisions are policy-driven: only advance traffic when region state is GREEN; run canaries in YELLOW with shadowing and accelerated telemetry; immediate rollback to previous variant when RED.
4) Provide explainability: each decision must surface contributing signals and thresholds in the console and the audit log.

Non-goals:
- Replace existing SLO/observability systems. This work complements them and reuses existing datastores/metrics.
- Implement new model evaluation infra from scratch (we will call the existing eval pipeline and the semantic regression suite).

High-level design:
- Compatibility Scorer Service: a lightweight microservice that computes per-variant per-region scores from a weighted sum of components: schema (20), tokenizer/detokenizer diffs (15), KV-cache signing/format (15), op/kernels compatibility heuristics (15), quantization/precision flags (10), historical regression risk (10), manual-blocklist adjustments (15). Scores are returned with a breakdown for explainability.

- Regional Safety Lattice: rules engine that maps compatibility score + capacity_headroom_pct + live_quality_vector -> {GREEN, YELLOW, RED}. Example policy: if score >= 85 and headroom >= 20% and semantic-delta < 2% -> GREEN. If score 65-85 or headroom 10-20% or semantic-delta 2-5% -> YELLOW. Otherwise -> RED. Policies are configurable per-customer/tier.

- Canary Controller Integration: the controller uses the lattice state to determine allowed actions:
  - GREEN: advance staged traffic per schedule; allow A/B splits; enable tail-off experiment windows.
  - YELLOW: only shadow traffic + low-rate canary (<=1%); collect extra semantic evals; require manual or automated mitigation plan to advance.
  - RED: auto-failover to previous variant in-region; if cross-region routing enabled, route traffic to nearest compatible region with GREEN and sufficient headroom; mark rollout blocked and create alert.

- Auto-rollback Arbiter: monitors rolling-window metrics and semantic-eval jobs. If any hard thresholds are crossed (P95 latency > 2x baseline, error rate delta > 0.5%, semantic-regression fail rate > 3%), the arbiter triggers rollback actions and annotates the audit trail with the scorer/lattice inputs.

- Observability & Audit: every decision is logged to the rollout-audit index with the scorer breakdown, lattice state, and metric snapshots. Console exposes a per-rollout "safety timeline" and decision inspector.

Acceptance criteria:
- Compatibility scorer prototype returns score + breakdown for all model variants used in our staging catalog.
- Safety lattice computes deterministic states and the canary controller honors states in staged rollout flows.
- Auto-rollback triggers on synthetic regression scenarios in the e2e harness and does not produce false positive rollbacks in control tests.
- Console displays decision breakdown for at least 30 days in the rollout timeline.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Overly conservative policies block benign rollouts. Mitigation: provide conservative default but allow team-specific relaxations and an override path with audit.
- Risk: Scorer latency adds tail to deployment flow. Mitigation: scorer is async-cached with precomputed scores during model onboarding; synchronous check is cached per-minute.

Rollout plan:
1) Week 1: Implement scorer schema + offline scoring of current variants and store results in rollout-store.
2) Week 2: Implement lattice engine and unit tests; add canary controller hooks in staging.
3) Week 3: Wire up arbiter and alerting; create e2e harness for semantic regression injection.
4) Week 4: Staged rollout in us-west-2 with one internal team; expand to eu-west-1 after validation.

Notes: the design intentionally treats "compatibility" as an orthogonal signal to quality metrics so teams can run aggressive hardware/quantization changes with explicit risk accounting.
